data.name: Delusion
data.detailed_description:
Delusion é um jogo de quebra-cabeça incomum que conta a história de um mundo lindo, cheio de vida e cores, que se tornou irreconhecível após uma série de eventos inexplicáveis.



Descobre a verdade, ajuda a restaurar o mundo e salva os seus habitantes numa viagem de cinco capítulos, com um total de cem puzzles novos e cuidadosamente elaborados para resolver. A jogabilidade por turnos é simples mas desafiante, com progressão de níveis satisfatória e sem temporizadores, que te permite relaxar e encontrar o próprio ritmo.



Surpreende-te com um estilo artístico único, desenhado maioritariamente à mão, com a atmosfera, a profundidade e a atenção aos detalhes do mundo vivo e respirável de Delusion.



  • Um estilo artístico único e maioritariamente desenhado à mão que dá vida ao mundo e à sua atmosfera inconfundível
  • Jogabilidade simples, mas desafiante, baseada em turnos, com uma progressão de nível satisfatória e sem temporizadores, que permite relaxar e encontrar o próprio ritmo
  • Um total de 100 puzzles cuidadosamente elaborados, cada um com um desafio opcional com um colecionável único oferecido como recompensa pela sua conclusão
  • Uma história intrigante contada em 5 capítulos, com suporte para progressão não linear do jogo
  • Trilha sonora original composta pelo premiado compositor Tomáš Vrána
  • Compatível com daltônicos

reviews.review:
Delusion is an atmospheric puzzle adventure developed and published by Silver Line Games that combines thoughtful turn-based challenges with a mysterious fantasy narrative. Rather than focusing on intense difficulty or fast-paced action, the game is built around exploration, environmental storytelling, and carefully designed puzzles that encourage observation and experimentation. Its greatest strength lies in how it merges gameplay and narrative into a cohesive journey, inviting players into a world that has been scarred by an unexplained disaster and asking them to gradually uncover the truth behind its downfall.

The game's story begins in a land that was once filled with color, life, and prosperity. Following a sequence of mysterious events, however, the world has become damaged and distorted, leaving its inhabitants struggling to understand what happened. As players progress through the adventure, they slowly piece together fragments of the world's history while helping restore balance to locations that have fallen into ruin. The narrative unfolds at a measured pace, allowing curiosity to drive the experience rather than relying on constant exposition or dramatic cutscenes.

One of the most appealing aspects of Delusion is its approach to puzzle design. The game features a large collection of handcrafted challenges spread across multiple chapters, each introducing new concepts while building upon previously learned mechanics. Rather than overwhelming players with complexity, the puzzles are designed to encourage logical thinking and experimentation. Solutions often require careful observation and planning, making every completed challenge feel rewarding without becoming frustrating.

The turn-based structure contributes significantly to the game's accessibility. Players are given as much time as they need to analyze situations and consider their next move. There are no countdown timers, reflex-based sequences, or pressure-inducing mechanics forcing immediate decisions. This slower pace allows players to fully engage with each puzzle and creates a relaxing atmosphere that distinguishes Delusion from many modern puzzle games focused on speed and efficiency.

The progression system benefits from the strong connection between gameplay and storytelling. Every puzzle solved contributes to the larger objective of understanding and repairing the world. This relationship gives each challenge narrative significance and prevents the puzzles from feeling disconnected from the adventure. Instead of simply advancing through a sequence of abstract levels, players feel as though they are actively participating in the world's recovery.

An additional layer of depth comes from optional objectives attached to the puzzles. These bonus challenges encourage players to think beyond basic solutions and experiment with alternative strategies. Completionists and puzzle enthusiasts will appreciate the opportunity to pursue perfect solutions and collect additional rewards, while players focused primarily on the story can continue progressing without feeling obligated to master every mechanic.

The visual presentation is one of the game's most impressive achievements. Delusion utilizes a distinctive hand-drawn art style that gives every environment a unique sense of personality. The contrast between beauty and decay is a recurring visual theme, with damaged landscapes serving as reminders of the catastrophe that transformed the world. The environments are filled with detail and atmosphere, creating locations that are not only visually appealing but also emotionally engaging.

The world itself possesses a dreamlike quality that enhances the sense of mystery. Many environments feel surreal and otherworldly, reinforcing the idea that something fundamental has changed. This artistic approach helps create an experience that feels both relaxing and unsettling, encouraging players to continue exploring in search of answers. The setting often communicates its story visually, rewarding players who pay attention to environmental details.

Sound design plays a crucial role in supporting the atmosphere. The original soundtrack complements the gameplay with gentle, emotional compositions that reinforce both the beauty and melancholy of the world. Rather than dominating the experience, the music quietly enhances exploration and puzzle-solving, helping establish a reflective mood that remains consistent throughout the adventure.

The game's pacing deserves particular praise. Delusion understands the value of gradual progression and never rushes players through its content. New mechanics are introduced carefully, allowing players to become comfortable with existing concepts before additional layers are added. This thoughtful structure keeps the experience engaging while avoiding the information overload that can sometimes affect puzzle-heavy games.

Exploration also contributes meaningfully to the overall experience. The world is divided into multiple chapters, each containing unique environments and challenges. Moving between these areas creates a strong sense of progression while continually introducing fresh visual themes and puzzle variations. The changing scenery helps maintain interest and reinforces the feeling of traveling through a living world rather than a collection of isolated levels.

The game's primary limitation is that players seeking highly demanding puzzle design or action-oriented gameplay may find the overall experience too relaxed. Delusion is intentionally focused on atmosphere, storytelling, and thoughtful problem-solving rather than intense challenge. However, this approach aligns perfectly with its creative vision and helps establish a distinctive identity within the puzzle genre.

What ultimately makes Delusion memorable is its ability to create an emotional connection through subtle storytelling and environmental design. The mystery of the world's collapse, combined with the gradual process of restoration, gives the adventure a sense of purpose beyond simply solving puzzles. Every completed challenge feels like a small step toward understanding a larger tragedy and helping a damaged world recover.

Delusion succeeds as both a puzzle game and a narrative experience. Its beautiful hand-drawn presentation, carefully crafted challenges, engaging mystery, and relaxing pace create an adventure that is easy to become immersed in. While it may not appeal to players looking for high-pressure gameplay or extreme difficulty, it offers a rewarding journey for those who appreciate thoughtful design, atmospheric storytelling, and creative puzzle solving.

Rating: 6/10
